qs.q: Patient blood groups and sex are examples of which level of measurement in SPSS?
qs.e: Nominal data represents categories with no meaningful order, such as blood group or sex. Ordinal data involves categories with a natural order.
qs.s: SPSS Statistical Analysis — HIT100 Course Notes: MCQs

qs.q: Which blood group is identified as having a relative risk susceptibility for developing cholera symptoms?
qs.e: Individuals with blood group type O have an increased incidence of cholera infection, while blood group AB offers relative protection. The relative susceptibility follows the order O greater than B greater than A greater than AB.

qs.q: Which historical figure discovered the ABO human blood groups in 1901, demonstrating that blood clumping is an immunological reaction?
qs.e: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO human blood groups in 1901 and established that blood clumping is an immunological reaction, earning him a Nobel prize. Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch are famous for other major microbiological discoveries rather than blood grouping.

qs.q: Which of the following blood groups has neither A nor B antigens on the surface of its red blood cells, but contains both a and b antibodies in its plasma?
qs.e: Blood group O lacks both A and B antigens on its red blood cells while possessing both a and b antibodies in the blood plasma. In contrast, blood group AB has both antigens and neither antibody.

qs.q: A patient experiences an unexpected drop in hemoglobin and mild jaundice approximately 7 days after receiving a blood transfusion. A direct antiglobulin test (DAT) is positive. Which blood group system is most notoriously associated with this type of delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction?
qs.e: The Kidd blood group system (Jka, Jkb antigens) is notoriously associated with delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions. Antibodies to Kidd antigens (anti-Jka, anti-Jkb) are often weak or undetectable in pre-transfusion testing but can rapidly increase after re-exposure, leading to extravascular hemolysis typically 3-10 days post-transfusion.
qs.s: Weekly Pathology Exam - October 16, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which blood group system is most frequently associated with delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions that present with a rapid drop in hemoglobin but negative initial antibody screens?
qs.e: The Kidd system is the classic cause of delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions. Antibodies fade quickly, screen negative, then surge after re-exposure causing rapid intravascular hemolysis.
qs.s: Master Immunohematology: Advanced Transfusion Medicine MCQs

ai.subject: Physiology
ai.summary: Blood groups are surface antigens on red cells that determine compatibility for transfusion and pregnancy. They arise from carbohydrate or protein differences encoded by ABO and Rh genes. Clinicians use group knowledge to prevent hemolysis and manage immune-mediated disease.

sections.p: The ABO system classifies red cells as A, B, AB or O based on the presence of A and B antigens; the Rh system adds D antigen positivity or negativity.
b: Naturally occurring anti‑A or anti‑B IgM antibodies develop early in life

sections.p: A and B antigens are carbohydrate chains added to the H antigen by specific glycosyltransferases. Rh D is a membrane protein that transports ions.
b: ABO genes on chromosome 9, Rh genes on chromosome 1
Antibodies are IgM and do not cross the placenta

sections.p: Expression of ABO enzymes is tissue‑specific; Rh D expression is regulated during erythropoiesis. No hormonal control is needed for antigen presence.
b: No known acute up‑ or down‑regulation

sections.p: Incompatible transfusion or pregnancy can trigger immune hemolysis. Auto‑ or allo‑antibodies may form after sensitisation (transfusion, pregnancy, transplantation).
b: Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction: fever, flank pain, dark urine
Hemolytic disease of the newborn (HDN): maternal anti‑D IgG crosses placenta

sections.p: Correct matching prevents life‑threatening hemolysis. Certain groups influence disease risk (e.g., severe malaria in O, thrombosis in non‑O).
b: Rh‑negative mother with Rh‑positive fetus → HDN
Group O higher risk of peptic ulcer disease

faq.q: Why can O‑negative blood be given to anyone in an emergency?
faq.a: It lacks A, B, and D antigens, so no pre‑formed antibodies in the recipient will react.

faq.q: What causes hemolytic disease of the newborn?
faq.a: Maternal IgG anti‑D (or anti‑A/B) crosses the placenta and destroys fetal red cells.

faq.q: Can a person change their blood group?
faq.a: No, ABO and Rh are genetically fixed; only acquired antibodies can change serology.
